question: Which exact operating-system and architecture matrix is included in the first vertical's build, packaging, recovery, IPC, WebView, browser, and Wasmtime conformance claims?
selected_option: Make Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on x86-64 with glibc the only first-vertical conformance and packaging target; retain portable boundaries for later macOS and Windows work without claiming them supported.
rationale: The user explicitly selected OPT-PLATFORM-LINUX-X64-FIRST. One native target gives the first vertical the smallest credible build, packaging, service, IPC, WebView, browser, and Wasmtime evidence matrix while preserving the daemon protocols and capability boundaries needed for later ports.

first_vertical_platform.claim_status: selected conformance target; not yet proven supported

required_semantics: only Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on x86-64 with glibc is inside the first-vertical build, package, install, startup, shutdown, crash-recovery, upgrade, IPC, WebView, browser-supervisor, WebAssembly-host, CLI and daemon conformance matrix
the selected platform must be proven on a native clean runner using exact pinned toolchain, dependency, system-library, WebView, JavaScript-runtime, Playwright-browser and Wasmtime identities

the service daemon remains the sole accepted-state transition authority and local clients use the selected Unix-domain-socket framed-JSON binding with platform-appropriate ownership and permission checks
the Tauri shell uses the platform WebView only as a thin client and requires Linux-specific CSP, protocol, window, packaging, install, launch and accessibility evidence

the Playwright supervisor and pinned first browser run as a separate least-privileged local process and require Linux-specific launch, sandbox, lifecycle, orphan-cleanup, artifact, redaction and crash evidence
the Wasmtime component host requires native x86-64 Linux evidence for component validation, import closure, capability denial, resource budgets, cancellation and recovery
SQLite durability, migration, backup, restore, contention and crash behavior are tested on the selected filesystem and process environment rather than inferred from library-level tests
platform support is claimed only after the complete selected matrix passes; a successful compile, package build, HTTP response, UI screenshot or isolated subsystem test is insufficient
portable protocol, storage, capability and supervisor boundaries must avoid encoding Linux-only semantics into canonical business meaning so later ports can supply different native bindings
non_implications: selecting a platform target does not prove that target supported, conformant, secure, performant, packaged, installable or releasable
this decision does not claim macOS, Windows, other Linux distributions, other architectures, containers or headless servers are supported
this decision does not choose exact Rust, Tauri, WebKitGTK, Node.js, Playwright, browser, Wasmtime, SQLite, linker, package-format or system-service versions
this decision does not authorize implementation, dependency installation, browser launch, remote exposure, publication, release, deployment or external effects

remaining_blockers: exact reproducible Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64 toolchain, dependency and system-library lock
package format, service integration, install, upgrade, rollback, signing and distribution bindings
numeric startup, latency, throughput, memory, storage, WebAssembly and browser resource budgets
Essays security-owner and Work Owner reviews for remote, WebAssembly and browser policies
Product Capability decision and dependent contracts
authored ontology closure and DomainSpec generation
deferred_decisions: macOS, Windows, additional Linux architectures and distributions require separate platform bindings and complete native conformance matrices before any support claim.
Exact package format, service manager unit, CPU baseline, system-library floor, WebView build and toolchain pins remain later implementation and release bindings.
